checks.claim: Model scope: all nonzero H:homog Gamma in d=1,2,3, 0<a<1, 0<alpha<d or alpha=d=1 (white endpoint), alpha+a<2; kappa=(4-alpha-a)/(3-alpha)>1; T_delta=delta^(-1/kappa); g_delta=delta^((1-a)/2); Gamma_delta=g_delta^2 Gamma stays in the admissible class
checks.reason: kappa>1 is equivalent to a<1 when alpha<3. A positive multiple of a nonnegative, even, positive-definite, homogeneous tempered Radon Gamma (including c*delta_0 when alpha=d=1) keeps the same alpha and a. delta->T_delta is a decreasing bijection from (0,1) onto (1,infinity). Zero covariance is set aside explicitly (see minor note).

checks.claim: Geometry: R_delta=L_delta+2 is the growing mask/data radius, separate from the shrinking physical radius T*delta. K_delta={0<=t<=L,|x|<=1+L-t} lies strictly inside B_R, and psi_delta=eta_R and m_delta=eta_R^2 both equal 1 on the needed region
checks.reason: K_delta is closed under backward cones: if |x|<=1+L-t and |y-x|<=t-s, then |y|<=1+L-s. Since 1+L<R, eta_R=1 on a neighbourhood of every backward base ball and every coefficient point. eta_R^2 is a valid zeta_R mask (even, smooth, in [0,1], equal to 1 on B_R, supported in B_2R) as required by actual-operator-driver and upper-gaussian GL. The mask is applied once, after heat smoothing. By physical_scale, r_T=T^((a-1)/(3-alpha)) tends to 0, so it is a different object from R_delta.

checks.claim: GC1 source law: with Y_fast(t,x)=delta^(a/2) Y_slow(delta t,x), the field g_delta Y_fast has the canonical source law for Gamma_delta, with heat width epsilon and Laplace cutoff eta_cut/delta
checks.reason: Change of variables gives K_eta(delta r)=delta^(-a) K_(eta/delta)(r), so delta^a K_eta(delta r)=K_(eta/delta)(r), matching raw-block Section 7. The covariance of g_delta Y_fast is therefore K_(eta/delta)(r) p_(2eps)*Gamma_delta, the Theorem-2 law for Gamma_delta at rho'=(eps,eta/delta). With delta fixed, rho' tends to 0 as (eps,eta) tends to 0, so source limits are taken before delta tends to 0.

checks.claim: GC1a: on the fixed-delta, fixed-rho source event, the E-source displacement v with data (eta_R,0) and coefficient m_delta g_delta Y_fast equals the unmasked ordinary solution u^full with data (1,0) throughout K_delta, and in particular on D at time L_delta
checks.reason: The planned route is sound. (1) b=m g Y_fast is compactly supported, smooth in space and continuous in time in every C^k norm. The Duhamel equation therefore has a unique solution in H^k x H^(k-1), which embeds in E. By uniqueness of the ordinary Duhamel equation it equals the actual source Young flow (fixed-mask-young Section 5), and its displacement is jointly continuous. (2) Free finite propagation must be applied to the TOTAL initial difference (eta_R-1,0). That difference is a constant plus a Schwartz phase, not an element of E, so the fixed-mask-young Section 2 compact-distribution matrix, including d=3 derivative and sphere entries, is the correct tool. It vanishes on K because eta_R-1 vanishes on an open neighbourhood of each backward base ball. (3) Inside K, m=1, so the difference w satisfies the positive-Green-measure Volterra equation with sample bound M, giving |w|<=sup_K|w| M^n L^(2n)/(2n)!, which tends to 0. No sign of the potential and no point trace are used. These are proof obligations that the target correctly lists; nothing in the statement fails.

checks.claim: GC1b: E|u^full(L,0)|^2 = v_d^(-1) E||v(L)||^2_(L2(D)), by unmasked source stationarity, joint measurability/Tonelli and finiteness, as an average of squares
checks.reason: F Section 4 supplies: locally continuous, jointly measurable versions; agreement with the L2 Picard sum at each fixed point; spatial stationarity of the unmasked u_rho; and the uniform bound Q_t. Combined with GC1a, Tonelli gives E int_D|v|^2 = int_D E|u^full(L,x)|^2 dx = v_d E|u^full(L,0)|^2 < infinity. The diagonal second moment is integrated, which avoids the square-of-average trap and any covariance-order reversal.

checks.claim: GC2a: apply F Section 5(11) separately to the full-source point limit for Gamma_delta, and actual E source/Young L2 convergence to the raw-flow displacement, on the same source law; the two limits match
checks.reason: F(11) depends only on the single-rho source law and its continuous version (F Section 1 and Section 5). It applies to the nonzero admissible Gamma_delta at t=L_delta with arbitrary-rate cutoffs, so the left side tends to E|u_(Gamma_delta)(L,0)|^2. On the other side, ||pr1(P^rho-P)z||_(L2(D)) <= ||(P^rho-P)z||_E. Fixed-horizon, fixed-radius all-Lp operator-difference convergence (fixed-mask-young Y3; raw-block Section 7(19)-(23) for the fast pullback, including the ordinary first-response identity) gives L2(Omega;L2(D)) convergence for the deterministic datum z_delta. Equal prelimits give equal limits. No pointwise raw phase evaluation is used.

The equality is direct-event (S)-(M) followed by the fast time change u=t/delta. sqrt(delta) W(delta u) equals g_delta W_fast as a distribution, with covariance |u-u'|^(-a) Gamma_delta. All mixed, self-pairing and empty chains and the d=3 Green-before-noise convention are included, as recorded at raw-block preceding (26). The inequality follows from ||f||_(L2(D)) <= ||f||_L2 <= ||f||_(H1/2) (Bessel weight Lambda=(1-Delta)^(1/2)), ||w||_E >= ||w_1||_(H1/2), and ||z_delta||_E = ||psi_delta||_(H1/2).

checks.claim: Fixed-delta finiteness: GL gives 1 <= E||P_delta^R||^2_(B(F)) < infinity for each fixed delta with R=R_delta, used only pointwise in delta and not as a rate along growing R
checks.reason: GL1 is stated for every R>0 and every delta in (0,1), so the single pair (delta,R_delta) is covered. Moving from B(F) to B(E) needs the restriction identity P_F i = i P_E. This follows from A i = i M_E (fixed-mask-young (3)), invariance of the range iE, and Young uniqueness; it gives ||P_E||_(B(E)) <= ||P_F||_(B(F)) because i is an isometry. The target flags this obligation. The E second moment is positive because P_E is invertible. The target explicitly forbids substituting the fixed-R GL rate along growing R_delta.

checks.claim: GC3a: ||psi_delta||^2_(H1/2) <= ||psi_delta||^2_(H1) = R^d||eta||_2^2 + R^(d-2)||grad eta||_2^2 <= C_eta R^d, and delta log(v_d^(-1) C_eta R_delta^d) tends to 0
checks.reason: With the unitary Fourier convention and weight <xi>^2: ||f(./R)||_2^2 = R^d||f||_2^2 and ||grad f(./R)||_2^2 = R^(d-2)||grad f||_2^2. Since R_delta>=3>1, R^(d-2)<=R^d. The prefactor is d delta log(1/delta+2)+O(delta), which tends to 0. The script's nine H1 rows and twelve prefactor rows agree, as a diagnostic only.

checks.claim: GC3b: limsup_T T^(-kappa) log E|u(T,0)|^2 <= limsup_delta delta log E||P_(delta,E)^(R_delta)||^2, as a conditional upper REDUCTION only
checks.reason: Take delta log of GC2b, use the bijection delta=T^(-kappa), and apply subadditivity of limsup. The data prefactor tends to 0, so no infinity-minus-infinity occurs. The right side is positive and finite at each delta, and an infinite limsup makes the bound trivial. The target asserts no uniform growing-R stochastic bound, no sharp constant and no source normalization.

minor: Notation: the driver is written 'A_E,R_delta(W_fast)', but in fixed-mask-young A_E=M_E L_psi lies in B(F,E). The E Young flow should be stated as driven by the B(E) driver g_delta M_E (equivalently i^(-1) A i), so it is not mistaken for the F-to-E column operator.

Line 86 says the E/F restriction identity must be checked 'if used'. It is in fact used: B(E) finiteness in GC2b/GC3b and the E-level source convergence in GC2a both rely on P_F i = i P_E and ||P_E|| <= ||P_F||. Record it as a definite later proof obligation.

GC1 leaves u^full's coefficient implicit. State that it is the unmasked g_delta Y_fast with data (1,0), and that F Sections 4-5 apply to this pullback through F Section 1's law-plus-continuous-version clause (as raw-block (25) did), not to the literal Theorem-2 Y_rho for Gamma_delta.

The inequalities ||f||_L2 <= ||f||_H1/2 <= ||f||_H1 and the formula ||psi||_H1^2 = ||psi||^2 + ||grad psi||^2 depend on the inhomogeneous Bessel weight Lambda=(1-Delta)^(1/2) with the unitary Fourier transform (actual-operator-driver Section 1). Stating that convention in GC3a would close the 'real data/complex norm conventions' item in worker-honesty.

Lean defines delta as a function of T. The target's inverse parametrization T_delta=delta^(-1/kappa), and the identity (delta^(-1/kappa))^(-kappa)=delta, is a routine rpow step outside the checked kernel facts. Note it as analytic.
The zero-covariance case is only 'may be handled separately'. It is trivial (u=1, and GC3b reduces to the free flow), but should be stated if all-model coverage is claimed for this reduction.
Taking k>d/2+1 in the higher-Sobolev identification is stronger than needed (k>d/2 suffices for continuity). This is harmless.
check-cone-v1.py asserts exact equality (good==1) on mpmath quadrature output, which is a fragile assertion. The JSON was not regenerated in this review.
